growthcleanr: a data cleaner for anthropometric measurements

Source: R/growthcleanr-package.R
growthcleanr-package.Rd

growthcleanr flags implausible anthropometric (height, weight, and head circumference) measurements in longitudinal datasets, such as those from electronic health records. It also identifies other measurements that should often be excluded from analyses.

Getting started

The main function is cleangrowth. Pass it a data frame with one row per measurement and columns subjid, param, agedays, sex, and measurement (plus an optional per-row id). Semi-wide and wide layouts, alternate column names, and date-of-birth / visit-date ages are also supported. growthcleanr will not delete or edit data: it returns your data with an added exclude column labeling each row "Include" or an exclusion code naming why it recommends exclusion.

The function growthcleanr_app opens a Shiny app that runs growthcleanr without writing code. A command-line driver is documented in vignette("command-line").

New to growthcleanr? Start with vignette("new-start-here"). See vignette("output") for more information including the returned columns and vignette("configuration") for the full index of arguments and thresholds.
